Initial Exploratory Data Analysis for STAT 551 Final Project

Author

Kyle Maher

Published

April 29, 2026

Setup

library(corrplot)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

Data

data <- read.csv("FP_Data.csv")
df <- as.data.frame(data)

EDA

names(df)
[1] "y"  "x1" "x2" "x3" "x4" "x5" "x6" "x7" "x8"

Correlations

corrplot(cor(select(df, -x8)))

Pairplot

pairs(select(df, -x8))

X1

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x1, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Pretty much random noise.

X2

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x2, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Pretty much random noise.

X3

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x3, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Slight positive correlation.

X4

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x4, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Strong positive correlation.

X5

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x5, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Strong negative correlation.

X6

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x6, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Slight positive correlation.

X7

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x7, y = y, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

Pretty much random noise.

X8

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x8, y = y, fill = x8)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )

As the classification increments (A-D) y tends to decrease.

  • Outlier in A at 100
  • Outlier in D at 0

y

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = y)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, aes(y = after_stat(density))) +
  stat_function(
    fun = dnorm,
    args = list(mean = mean(df$y), sd = sd(df$y)),
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 1
  )
df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = y, fill = x8)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10) +
  facet_wrap(~x8)
  • A right skewed
  • D left skewed
xtabs(~x8, df)
x8
 A  B  C  D 
67 50 38 45

Grouped Histograms

df %>%
  filter(x8 == "A" | x8 == "C") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = y)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = ("Distribution of y when x8 is B or D")
  )
df %>%
  filter(x8 == "B" | x8 == "D") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = y)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of y when x8 is B or D"
  )

Checking Multicolinearity

x3 & x4

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x3, y = x4, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

x4 & x5

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x4, y = x5, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()

x6 & x7

df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = x6, y = x7, color = x8)) +
  geom_point()
  • Wacky \(cos(x)\) function here

Baseline Model

baseline_model <- lm(y ~ ., data = df)
summary(baseline_model)
